headline: THE ROUND IS CORRECT AND I TRIED HARD TO REFUTE IT. R12-B1 IS CLOSED AT ITS CAUSE AND THE CLOSURE IS PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: the arming flag is GONE, and I verified the replacement claim with strace ground truth rather than by reading the tracer - on every hand-off, on a seeded tree, on a detached worktree and with the measured tree as the process CWD, the FIRST in-tree openat of the child is .warp/__pycache__/validate.cpython-312.pyc (the first owner load, which follows the install line), execve count is 1 so no child's opens are missed, and the set of in-tree FILE opens strace saw is EXACTLY the set the hook reported - MISSED: NONE, EXTRA: NONE, both directions, both gates. THE NEW NON-BLINDNESS TEST SURVIVED FOUR MUTATIONS, each run as a whole selftest in a detached worktree: (M1) install moved one line later -> 2 failures; (M2) the ARMED flag restored with the install line left exactly where it is, so every textual conjunct still passes -> the 16-cell matrix alone caught it, 1 failure; (M3) the recorded event set narrowed to silently drop the probe path -> 1 failure; (M4) the enumerated expectation replaced by dict(_M10_R13_BLIND), i.e. self-derived from the very code path it checks, AND the flag restored -> STILL 1 failure, because the three named-list conjuncts at scripts/selftest.py:19832-19837 are independent of the expectation dict. An assertion that passes when the property is broken is worse than none; this one does not. R12-B2 and R12-B3 are closed BY MEASUREMENT: a9e808e is 58 files / 2925 / 545 by both --shortstat and a numstat sum, the round-13 fix commit is 9 / 211 / 74, 063c33b..2e047b6 is 62 / 3146 / 620, and my own instrumented selftest at the evidence commit printed engines=90 pyruns=427 - the published absolutes EXACTLY, with 16-11=5 and 64-50=14 closing. ALL EIGHT REPUBLISHED TRACE COUNTS REPRODUCE TO THE PATH: seeded 25 / 18 / 10 / 53 and a warm detached worktree at the FIX commit 9 / 445 / 146 / 221, with the working tree at 446 exactly as the manifest says and warns. THE THREE LIVE DESIGN FINDINGS ARE ALL REFUTED ON THE SHIPPED CODE, not argued away: the real no-argument path renders 2 authenticated incidents and four real measures; the diagnosability score FAILS in five independent ways I constructed; and AC5/AC6 are not mutually exclusive as built. GATE GREEN at 3173/0. THE VERDICT IS pass_with_notes rather than pass for ONE reason, and it is a scope word in a shipped docstring rather than a hole in the guarantee: the hook records the `open' audit event only, so 270 of the 722 in-tree openats on the corpus hand-off are O_DIRECTORY (scandir/listdir) and five of them - proof, proof/WARP-X, plans, .warp/decisions, specs - lie OUTSIDE the declared roots and are asserted against by nothing. I spent the rest of the review trying to turn that into a blocker and FAILED: 15 hostile shapes at those five paths produced zero hangs, zero tracebacks and exit 0 on all four surfaces, and plans/ and .warp/decisions/ render BYTE-IDENTICALLY whether present, absent or a FIFO, so no number moves. Round 12's reviewer examined this exact primitive set and ruled it correct; my measurements confirm the ruling. It is a note.

notes: Ranked by six-month impact. 1. THE PATTERN THAT COST TWELVE ROUNDS HAS BROKEN, and I want that on the record before the note that follows it, because it is the finding. Rounds 8 through 12 each failed on the same shape: the DESIGN was one boundary short, or the PROOF of the design was exhibited over a convenient slice. Round 13 does neither. It closes the slice at its cause (no flag, no phase), and then - this is the new thing - it makes the PROOF MECHANISM ITSELF the subject of a differential with an enumerated expectation and a mutant that is the previous round's own defect. That is the first time in this item's history that the instrument has been measured instead of described, and it is the reason I could not find a thirteenth boundary: I attacked the instrument for most of this review and it held under four mutations, including one that neutralized its own expectation. The method lesson generalizes past WARP-1210 and belongs in the WARP corpus: WHEN A PROOF IS THE DELIVERABLE, THE PROOF NEEDS A MUTANT THAT IS THE LAST KNOWN BLINDNESS, AND THE EXPECTATION MUST BE ENUMERATED SOMEWHERE THE MEASURED CODE CANNOT REACH. 2. THE ONE THING I WOULD CHANGE, AND IT IS A SCOPE WORD RATHER THAN A HOLE. .warp/metrics_read_closure.py:28-30 says the selftest `asserts that no path opened INSIDE THE TREE lies outside the declared roots'. The hook records the `open' audit event only. On the corpus hand-off I measured 722 in-tree openat syscalls of which 270 carry O_DIRECTORY - directory enumerations through os.scandir/os.listdir, which raise the `os.scandir' audit event and not `open' - and five distinct in-tree paths among them (proof, proof/WARP-X, plans, .warp/decisions, specs) match NO declared root of that hand-off and are asserted against by nothing. In Python's own vocabulary a directory enumerated with scandir was not `opened', and round 12's reviewer examined this exact primitive set and ruled it correct because only an OPEN blocks; my measurements confirm the ruling from both directions (see the residual). But the module is the artifact an adopter reads, and it does not say which primitive set the word covers. THE FIX IS FIVE WORDS AND IT IS THE SAME KIND OF FIX ROUND 13 JUST MADE TWICE: say `no path OPENED (the interpreter `open' audit event: builtin open, os.open, io.open_code, io.FileIO; directory ENUMERATION is a different event and cannot block) inside the tree ...', and add the primitive set to assumption 5 as a FOURTH declared limit beside the fixture set, the out-of-tree discard and the wedged regular file. I did NOT make this a blocker because the harm is unreachable through it and no rendered number moves, both measured, and because the standing instruction is that an overstated sentence is DELETED rather than argued about across rounds. It should be done at the next touch of this module, not in a fourteenth round of its own. 3. THE THREE PRE-BUILD DESIGN FINDINGS WERE ALL GOOD CRITICISM OF THE SPEC AND ARE ALL DEAD AGAINST THE BUILD, and the gap between those two facts is itself worth recording. Arm A's F6 (nobody constructs the real readers) was the sharpest thing either arm found and it is exactly the failure mode that survives a green gate - but .warp/metrics.py:367 and .warp/dashboard.py:148 do construct them, and I proved the wiring end to end rather than by reading it. Arm B's F7/(c) (the diagnosability conjuncts cannot be false) is false against the shipped reader in five distinct ways I built. The lesson for the SPEC process rather than for this item: both arms were reviewing a document that genuinely did not name its call sites or its falsifiability, and a build that happened to do the right thing does not retire the criticism - PLAN-0012's spec template should require the wiring criterion and the falsifiability direction that arm A and arm B each asked for, because the next item's builder may not volunteer them. 4. TWO COSMETIC ITEMS I CHECKED AND AM NOT MAKING FINDINGS OF, listed so the next reviewer does not spend the time I did. (a) The parenthetical `which is why the first is the largest' beside the seeded counts 25 / 18 / 10 / 53 is FALSE if `largest' means the largest count (53 > 25) and TRUE if it means the largest CHANGE from round 12's 4 / 14 / 3 / 46 (+21 against +4, +7, +7). I measured both readings; the sentence's own subject is what arming from the start CHANGED, which is the true reading, so I rule it ambiguous rather than false and suggest deleting five words at the next touch. (b) The manifest's `round' field is the STRING "13" where round 12's was the INTEGER 12. Nothing validates it (PROOF_REQ does not list it) and the gate is green either way, but the two proof records for one item now disagree on the type of a field a future query will read. 5. WHAT I COULD NOT BREAK, said plainly because the instruction to default to refuting makes silence ambiguous. I could not find a phase in front of the hook (strace, four hand-offs, three trees, cwd-inside and cwd-outside, execve==1). I could not find a primitive that escapes it and can wedge (15 hostile shapes at the five invisible paths, zero hangs, zero tracebacks, exit 0 on all four surfaces, and byte-identical renders across present/absent/FIFO for plans and .warp/decisions). I could not make the blindness matrix pass while the property was broken (four mutations, four failures). I could not find a figure that does not reproduce (thirteen line counts, three numstats, eight trace counts, engines=90, pyruns=427, and the four stderr byte counts of the pass-module residual, which I confirmed are path-length dependent and land on 854/500 and 747/395 at root path lengths of 41 and 40 - I measured the scaling at three path lengths to be sure they were real measurements rather than invented). And I could not make the diagnosability score render 100 percent on an input that does not deserve it.

residual_rulings.NEW (mine, ruled here rather than left f: TRADEOFF, and I ruled it BY ATTACK from both directions rather than by accepting the primitive set. MEASURED: `strace -f -e trace=openat,open,execve' over the shipped tracer with the measured tree as cwd gives 722 in-tree openats on spec_corpus, 270 of them O_DIRECTORY, against 446 reported by the hook; the difference is exactly the directory enumerations, and the five distinct in-tree paths among them - proof, proof/WARP-X, plans, .warp/decisions, specs - match no declared root of that hand-off component by component. IF the hook recorded os.scandir the undeclared list would be NON-EMPTY, so the event filter is load-bearing for the assertion passing at all, and that is why I treated it as a candidate blocker. IT IS NOT ONE, on two independent measurements. FIRST, THE HARM IS UNREACHABLE: I put a FIFO, a symlink loop and mode-000 at each of those five paths (15 configurations) and drove the four real surfaces as processes under a 12-second clock - ZERO hangs, ZERO tracebacks, exit 0 with non-empty stdout in all 60 runs, and the three paths that are declared read units or their parents were NAMED in the output. The mechanism is structural rather than lucky: os.scandir/os.listdir issue openat with O_DIRECTORY|O_NONBLOCK, which returns ENOTDIR on a FIFO and ELOOP on a symlink loop instead of blocking, so an enumeration cannot produce the infinite block this item's declared class turns on. SECOND, NO NUMBER MOVES: I compared the four surfaces byte for byte across plans PRESENT, plans ABSENT and plans as a FIFO, and again for .warp/decisions, and all twelve renders are byte-identical to each other and to baseline - those roots feed no rendered support figure, so there is no silent degradation of a published number either. THIRD, IT IS NOT A NEW LIMIT: the round-12 reviewer probed the interpreter, established that `open' fires for builtin open, os.open, io.open_code, io.FileIO and read_text but not for listdir/scandir/stat, and ruled that `the right primitive set for the harm, because only an OPEN blocks on a FIFO' - a ruling recorded in a committed verdict, which my measurements confirm rather than overturn. WHAT REMAINS IS THE SENTENCE AND THE DECLARATION, and that is note 2: the word `opened' in .warp/metrics_read_closure.py:28-30 does not name its primitive set, and assumption 5 lists three remaining limits without listing this one. Fix the five words and add the fourth limit at the next touch of the module.
residual_rulings.RESIDUAL 1 (assumptions[2]) - the corpus: TRADEOFF, carried unchanged and re-ruled on the owner's own test. The alternative is worse in the direction this item exists to protect: the owner opens those roots with a bare read_text() and a whole-file read of a FIFO blocks forever, so the choice is refuse-and-name or wedge-four-surfaces-in-silence. I re-measured the refuse path this round as a side effect of the directory attack above - a FIFO at proof/ and at proof/WARP-X/ both produce exit 0 with the source NAMED on all four surfaces where round 11 hung. The narrower rule needs a static heuristic over an owner's code, which is the guess this item has been failed for three times. Over-broad and NAMED beats narrow and silent.
residual_rulings.RESIDUAL 2 (assumptions[3]) - the organ: TRADEOFF, unchanged, and I hit it from a direction the declaration invites: a FIFO at .warp/entropy.py on a real detached worktree left all four surfaces ALIVE (exit 0) with a much larger stdout than baseline, which is the organ sweep naming it rather than the loader blocking on it. The declared exception holds too - an ABSENT cache is not refused, because nothing opens what is not there.
residual_rulings.RESIDUAL 3 (assumptions[4]) - two roots: TRADEOFF, re-measured rather than cited, on a REAL tree rather than a seeded one. I put a FIFO at scripts/check_pack_drift.py and at plugin/templates/scripts/runners/cli/cli_runner.py in a detached worktree at 1c8c747 - both are area source files the contract's own includes expand to - and all four surfaces exited 0 with non-empty stdout both times, so entropy's is_file() filter really does stand in front of the open. The second half is arithmetic rather than measurement and it is sound: an O_CREAT|O_EXCL open of an existing entry fails rather than blocking, which is what makes importlib's cache-write path safe.

disposition: LAND IT. This is the round that closes WARP-1210, and I say that as the thirteenth reviewer of an item where rounds 8 through 12 each found a real defect and where a rubber-stamp pass would cost exactly as much as a rubber-stamp fail. THE THREE BLOCKERS ARE CLOSED AT THEIR CAUSE AND I VERIFIED EACH ONE THE HARD WAY. R12-B1: the arming flag is gone rather than moved, and I did not accept the replacement claim - I took strace ground truth over ten runs across three trees including the case where the measured tree is the process cwd, and the first in-tree openat is always the first owner load, execve is always 1, and the hook's coverage of in-tree FILE opens is EXACT in both directions. R12-B2 and R12-B3: every replacement figure reproduces, including engines=90 and pyruns=427 from my own instrumented run, and the manifest now names the revision each figure describes, which was the real remedy. AND THE THING THAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM THE TWELVE ROUNDS BEFORE IT: the proof mechanism is now itself under test, with an enumerated expectation and a mutant that is the previous round's own blindness, and it SURVIVED FOUR MUTATIONS - including the one that matters most, in which I restored the ARMED flag while leaving the install line byte-for-byte where round 13 put it so that every textual conjunct still passed, and the behavioural 16-cell matrix caught it alone; and including the tautology test in which I replaced the enumerated expectation with the measurement itself and the three named-list conjuncts still failed the gate. THE THREE LIVE DESIGN FINDINGS ARE ALL DEAD AGAINST THE BUILD, measured rather than argued: the real no-argument path renders two authenticated incidents and four real measures on a tree with real files (arm A's F6 refuted at .warp/metrics.py:367 and .warp/dashboard.py:148); the diagnosability score falls to 50 percent in five independent ways I constructed, two of them falsifying the conjunct arm B calls true by construction (arm B's F7 refuted); and AC5 and AC6 are simultaneously satisfied and separately asserted, with AC6's byte-identity proven against git history rather than a pin and its render half asserted as byte-exact prefix preservation (arm B's (d) refuted). WHY pass_with_notes AND NOT pass. One scope word in a shipped docstring. .warp/metrics_read_closure.py:28-30 claims the trace asserts that no path opened inside the tree lies outside the declared roots; the hook records the `open' audit event only, and I measured 270 O_DIRECTORY openats on the corpus hand-off of which five in-tree paths lie outside the declared roots with nothing asserting against them. I spent the back half of this review trying to make that a blocker and could not: 60 surface runs across 15 hostile shapes at those five paths produced zero hangs, zero tracebacks and exit 0, because scandir issues O_DIRECTORY|O_NONBLOCK and cannot block; and twelve renders across present/absent/FIFO for two of those roots are byte-identical, so no number moves. Round 12's reviewer examined this exact primitive set and ruled it correct; my measurements confirm the ruling rather than overturn it. So it is a sentence that does not name its primitive set and a fourth limit missing from assumption 5 - fix five words at the next touch of the module, do not spend a fourteenth round on it. That is the whole of my reservation, and under the standing rule that an overstated sentence is deleted rather than argued about, and that the round cap kills the argument about wording while never excusing a defect, this item is done. The design has been right since round 12 and the proof of it is now right too.
